name: ttconv
role: Python library and CLI for converting timed-text subtitle and caption formats
notes: 2026-11-15: Assess because deterministic conversion to delivery caption formats fills a distinct gap beyond subtitle authoring and burn-in. Revisit after checking standards conformance coverage.
2026-11-15: Assessment uncertainty: official pages read did not establish release recency; verify the exact licence text and standards coverage before promotion.

evidence.result: Hand-written SRT with 3 cues (1 two-line, 1 italic) converted to WebVTT and TTML; all 16 predeclared checks pass: 3 cues, timings 1000-2500, 3120-5040, 5500-7250 ms, text and line breaks, TTML well-formed in the TTML namespace, WebVTT back to SRT keeps timings; second conversion byte-identical. Python 3.12.2, macOS arm64.
evidence.scope: SRT (3 cues, 2-line, italic) to WebVTT and TTML: cues, ms timings, text, breaks, well-formed TTML namespace, VTT to SRT round-trip; no IMSC profile; macOS arm64.

summary: Python library and `tt` command-line tool for converting timed-text files across formats including STL, SRT, TTML, SCC and WebVTT. It automates format conversion; standards conformance and preservation of format-specific features need workflow-specific checks.
use_when: Convert timed-text captions between supported delivery formats
Choose scripted conversion over authoring captions from scratch
avoid_when: Use subtitle-editing tools for interactive timing and text authoring
Use FFmpeg subtitle filters to burn captions into video
